top_stories.title: Elsevier Expands LeapSpace & Sets Up AI Advisory Board
top_stories.summary: Elsevier has expanded its LeapSpace platform, positioning it as a research-grade AI foundation built on the world's largest collection of highly cited scientific research. The company has also established an independent AI advisory board to oversee the platform's development. The move signals a significant push by a major academic publisher into governed, research-specific AI infrastructure.

top_stories.title: OpenAI Creates a New Framework to Disclose Bad AI Behavior [Metered]
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has released a new policy framework for reporting incidents of model misalignment, establishing a structured process for disclosing cases where AI models behave in unintended or harmful ways. The framework is designed to improve transparency and accountability around model behaviour. It represents one of the more formal industry attempts to systematise misalignment reporting.

top_stories.title: Claude Comes for Gemini with Its Own Take on Docs and Slides
top_stories.summary: Anthropic has launched new document and presentation creation features within Claude, bringing it into direct competition with Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot in productivity AI. The new capabilities are part of the Claude One offering and allow users to create and edit structured documents and slides natively within the Claude interface. The move marks a significant expansion of Anthropic's product ambitions beyond pure chat and API services.

top_stories.title: OpenAI Reimagining Advertising with AI
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a post outlining its vision for transforming the advertising industry using AI, exploring how generative models can reshape ad creation, targeting, and measurement. The piece signals OpenAI's intent to move further into the advertising market, a sector with significant commercial implications. It follows broader industry interest in applying large language models to marketing and brand communications.

top_stories.title: Mistral X Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing
top_stories.summary: Mistral AI has announced a partnership with Mozilla to bring private, multilingual AI capabilities to browsing. The collaboration aims to integrate Mistral's language models into Mozilla's ecosystem in a privacy-preserving way, with support for multiple languages. The partnership positions both organisations as alternatives to Big Tech AI browser integrations.

further_links.title: Washington Won't Be Regulating AI Anytime Soon [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports that prospects for federal AI regulation in the US remain dim, with political and legislative conditions making near-term action unlikely.

further_links.title: How to Connect AI Usage to Business Value
further_links.summary: OpenAI outlines frameworks and strategies for organisations to measure and demonstrate the business value generated by their AI deployments.

further_links.title: How Workers Are Unlocking New Ways of Working
further_links.summary: OpenAI publishes research and case studies on how employees across industries are adapting their workflows and finding productivity gains through AI tools.

further_links.title: Google Will Now Let Any AI Agent Run Your Smart Home
further_links.summary: Google has announced MCP integration for Google Home, enabling any compatible AI agent to control smart home devices through a standardised interface.

further_links.title: Microsoft's Commitment for AI in Education
further_links.summary: Microsoft has published commitments around AI use in education, focusing on student protection and strengthening learning outcomes through responsible AI deployment.

further_links.title: Cloudflare: Stay Discoverable in Search While Disallowing AI Training
further_links.summary: Cloudflare has introduced tooling that allows website owners to block AI training crawlers while remaining visible to standard search engine indexing.

further_links.title: A Brief History of AI Executives Calling for Regulation
further_links.summary: The Verge traces the pattern of AI industry leaders publicly advocating for regulation, examining the gap between those calls and actual policy outcomes.

further_links.title: China Isn't Buying Silicon Valley's Call for an AI Slowdown [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports that Chinese AI developers and officials are dismissing calls from US tech leaders for a slowdown in AI development, framing it as a competitive advantage play.

further_links.title: Helping Older Adults Use AI in Everyday Life
further_links.summary: OpenAI details initiatives aimed at making AI tools more accessible and useful for older adults, including partnerships and product design considerations.

further_links.title: The AI Data Center E-Waste Problem Is Huge
further_links.summary: The Verge examines the growing environmental challenge posed by hardware turnover in AI data centres, as rapid model iteration drives accelerating equipment disposal.
